topStory.headline: NSF Selects 25 Faculty for Inaugural A.I. Education Fellows Program
topStory.summary:
Winston Wu, an assistant professor at the University of Hawaii at Hilo, has been selected as one of 25 faculty nationwide for the NSF's inaugural NAIRR A.I. Education Fellows program, according to the University of Hawaii at Hilo. The fellowship runs through February 2027 and includes a $5,000 stipend. Fellows are tasked with piloting courses using NSF A.I. resources, supporting faculty integration nationwide, and helping shape strategic direction for the national project.

The NAIRR Pilot Classroom project aims to create "a national initiative dedicated to building a sustainable community of practice for advancing A.I. education for all." Wu's expertise spans natural language processing and machine learning with a focus on multilingual and low-resource applications, particularly supporting language revitalization efforts in local communities.

Wu stated his goal to "build technologies that benefit the local community." He teaches courses ranging from introductory programming to advanced natural language processing and deep learning, while coaching competitive programming teams. The fellowship structure involves a year-long commitment with national visibility and peer collaboration rather than one-time workshops or isolated pilot programs.

stories.headline: Google Launches A.I. Fellowship for University Faculty
stories.summary: Google announced a Higher Education Faculty A.I. Fellowship targeting instructors already using A.I. in teaching or research, according to EdTech Innovation Hub. The program focuses on solving institutional challenges like assessment design and policy development, with participants working on specific impact challenges at their schools. Applications require portfolios of A.I. work and include an in-person component in London.

stories.headline: Hirezon Launches A.I. Tools for Higher Ed Recruitment
stories.summary: Higher education HR technology provider Hirezon introduced A.I. Suites, starting with A.I. Candidate Summary that analyzes application materials and generates structured summaries for search committees, according to HRTech Series. The company reports 30-40% reduction in review time and plans additional A.I. tools for college and university hiring processes.

stories.headline: Babson Professor Explores When Students Should Struggle in A.I. Age
stories.summary: Writing professor Kristi Girdharry at Babson College advocates for moments when students work without A.I. to develop their own thinking before learning to use tools strategically, according to Babson College. Her approach includes comparing A.I.-assisted and unassisted drafts to build student discernment about when shortcuts help versus hinder learning.

stories.headline: Old Dominion University Hosts A.I. Developments Webinar March 24
stories.summary: ODU's Research Institute for Digital Innovation in Learning will present "What Is New in Artificial Intelligence? Developments and Faculty Research in Higher Education" on March 24, according to Old Dominion University. The session examines current A.I. developments and highlights faculty research on generative A.I. in teaching and learning.

stories.headline: Stanford Researchers Challenge Five A.I. Education Myths
stories.summary: Stanford Accelerator for Learning experts addressed common misconceptions about A.I. in education, arguing that A.I. will not replace teachers, cheating concerns should drive assessment reform, and intentional design can support creativity, according to Stanford Report. The research emphasizes that banning A.I. is less effective than teaching responsible use and A.I. literacy.

stories.headline: Penn State Launches A.I. Literacy Framework
stories.summary: Penn State introduced an A.I. Literacy Framework as part of its A.I. Transformation Initiative, establishing four core competencies: technical knowledge, ethical awareness, critical thinking, and practical use, according to Penn State University. The framework was developed by working groups focused on undergraduates, graduate students, faculty, and staff, with resources available through University Libraries.
